quizzes.stem: A sales rep's private Project holds a price list saved as a file in March. Finance revises that list every month in a cloud-hosted document, and the rep keeps quoting March figures. What is the best fix?

options.a: Add each month's file next to the old ones and keep every one of them in view
options.b: Tell the instructions to favour whichever figure looks most recent in the files
options.c: Ask Claude to mention any figure it feels unsure about at the end of each reply
options.d: Swap the snapshot for a synced Drive link that tracks each new edition

explanation.d: A synced document follows its source, so the next read gets the latest version (connecting a document instead of copying it).
explanation.b: Ruled out because "an instruction is a request and a deleted file is a guarantee", and the old figure would still be in the knowledge base.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "nothing alerts you when a file goes stale", so Claude has no reason to doubt a March figure and the stale file stays in place.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Two versions of one document side by side invite Claude to quote either".

quizzes.stem: In March a colleague pastes the refund percentage into a Project's instructions. In June the policy changes, the team deletes the March policy file and uploads the June one, yet July replies still quote the March percentage. What explains it?

options.a: An earlier figure lives on in the standing rules, which the swap never touched
options.b: Memory carried the March percentage over from an earlier conversation
options.c: Retrieval over a large knowledge base returned an older passage than the June file
options.d: Sharing the Project keeps showing members the percentage they saw first

explanation.a:
Instructions say how to work and files say what is true, so a figure typed into the instructions is a
   second copy that no file update will touch (the first trap).
explanation.b:
Ruled out because memory "holds preferences
   and context that Claude picked up, not the authoritative text of a policy".
explanation.c:
Ruled out because the team
   deleted the March file, and "a deleted file is a guarantee" that no older passage remains to retrieve.
explanation.d:
is ruled
   out because "anyone with access can read the instructions and every file in the knowledge base" describes who
   sees the content, not whether it is current.

quizzes.stem: An operations lead supports several outside organisations, whose background material and house rules must never mix. Which set-up fits?

options.a: One Project, with each organisation's work kept in a chat of its own
options.b: One Project, with each organisation's rules headed by its name in the instructions
options.c: A Project apiece, each holding only its own instructions and reference files
options.d: Plain chats outside Projects, with memory keeping each organisation's details

explanation.c: Each Project is a self-contained space, so "one Project's context does not leak into another" (the memory paragraph).
explanation.b: Ruled out because instructions are "Standing rules every chat in the Project starts with", so headings by name still put every organisation's rules into every chat.
explanation.a: Ruled out because a Project lets you "hold focused chats that start with all of that already in view", so a chat of its own still sees every organisation's files and rules.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "memory is not a substitute for a knowledge file" and holds preferences, not each organisation's authoritative documents.

quizzes.stem: A consultant must hand a client a one-page dashboard that the client will open, adjust and forward. The consultant also wants to try a different layout without losing the first. Which approach fits?

options.a: An inline reply, with each design pasted into a fresh chat and compared by eye
options.b: A skill, with each design saved as its own custom skill in the account
options.c: An artifact, with each design kept in a separate branch of the same chat
options.d: A Project, with each new layout written in turn into its instructions

explanation.c:
An artifact opens in its own panel for editing and sharing, and editing an earlier message branches the
   chat so "each branch has its own artifact".
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "A short answer stays inline in the
   chat", and a dashboard the client will open and adjust is not a short answer.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because a skill is "A
   repeatable procedure used across many chats", not a deliverable the client can open.
explanation.d:
is ruled out because
   "Project instructions apply to every chat in that Project", so each new layout written there replaces the first
   for every chat and leaves no file for the client to open.

quizzes.stem: A consultant writes client briefings in one house layout, in unrelated chats, some inside Projects and some outside any Project. Which feature lets all of those chats follow the layout?

options.a: Written rules in one Project's own instructions
options.b: A plugin installed for the consultant's role
options.c: An artifact kept as the pattern for each briefing
options.d: A custom skill kept in the account's skill list

explanation.d:
A skill is a reusable procedure that Claude pulls in "in any chat where it is enabled", inside or outside
   a Project, and a simple one needs no code.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "Project instructions apply to every chat in that Project", and the consultant's
   other chats sit elsewhere.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "Where a skill is one playbook, a plugin is several", so a
   role's bundle is the wrong size for one layout.
explanation.c:
Ruled out because an artifact is "A document, deck, dashboard or small tool to hand
   to someone" and does not make later chats follow a layout.

quizzes.stem: A colleague shares a ZIP file of a "free time-saving skill" from an unknown site and asks you to upload it. What is the best response?

options.a: Read the instructions file inside, and upload it if nothing looks harmful
options.b: Decline the archive and ask for a copy from a source you already trust
options.c: Hold off until the colleague has run it for a week without trouble
options.d: Upload it to a test chat and judge it by the first reply it gives

explanation.b: Skills carry instructions and scripts that Claude follows, so the page says to install skills only from trusted sources and to review what they bundle.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "A skill can carry scripts and instructions that Claude follows", and reading the instructions alone leaves any scripts unchecked.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a skill from an unknown source is "a route for prompt injection", and a quiet week of use neither changes the source nor reveals hidden instructions.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the first reply cannot show hidden scripts or instructions, which is why the page says to review "code dependencies and bundled resources" first.

quizzes.stem: A manager links the company's cloud storage, then asks Claude to summarise a restricted finance directory. Claude cannot find it, although an administrator colleague sees it in the same storage. What explains this?

options.a: The tool carries the signed-in person's rights, which exclude that location
options.b: The tool is set to need approval, which holds back reading until a click
options.c: The workspace holding the chat must be shared before the area becomes visible
options.d: The area is too big for retrieval to cope with in a single request

explanation.a: "Claude inherits each person's permissions from the connected service", so the manager's reach, not the administrator's, decides what appears.
explanation.b: Ruled out because an organisation can "let Claude read a system and require a human click before it writes to it", so an approval rule asks for a click and does not hide a location.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system", not by sharing a workspace.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "a missing result often means the person cannot see the file", and size is not a cause it names.

quizzes.stem: A company connects its helpdesk to Claude. Agents may read tickets and add internal notes freely, but ending a ticket must wait for a person's click, and trainees must not see escalated tickets. Which design meets both rules?

options.a: Require approval to close, and write the group's limit into the connector's instructions
options.b: Require approval to close, and give trainees a custom connector of their own
options.c: Require approval to close, and leave the group's limit in the source system itself
options.d: Require approval to close, and hide those tickets with a Claude tool setting

explanation.c: Each tool can be set to need approval, and Claude inherits each person's permissions, so a restriction on one group belongs in the source system.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system,
   by changing who can open what, not by rewording an instruction".
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "Claude inherits
   each person's permissions from the connected service", so a second connector still shows a trainee every ticket
   their helpdesk account can open.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Owners can set what the tools may do", which acts on tools and not on which tickets a person may open.

quizzes.stem: A team lead finds a handy link on a forum that would add a custom connector in seconds. What is the best step?

options.a: Install it, then watch the first few replies for anything odd
options.b: Install it only after checking the forum thread's ratings and replies
options.c: Install it only after checking its operator and the scopes it requests
options.d: Install it only after checking that the plan allows a custom connector

explanation.c: The checklist says to connect only to servers from trusted organisations and to read the scopes before approving them.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Anything outside the directory is untrusted until you have reviewed who runs it", and forum ratings are not that review.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Remote tools can change after you approve them", so a good first reply proves nothing about later behaviour.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "a custom connector has not been verified by Anthropic", whatever the plan allows.

quizzes.stem: A recruiter's private Project answers hiring questions from a policy that HR revises each quarter in a shared drive. The recruiter wants answers that stay current and can be traced. Which design fits?

options.a: Upload a copy now, and note a review date at the top of the instructions
options.b: Sync the source document, and ask in the instructions for the file it used
options.c: Type the policy wording into the instructions, since those are always read
options.d: Keep the policy in memory, and ask Claude to quote it with its source

explanation.b: A synced document follows its source, and "A reply that names the file it used shows at once when it used an old one" (page 1).
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an uploaded file is a copy as of the day you uploaded it", and a review date does not make a reply name its source.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A figure typed into the instructions is a second copy that no file update will touch".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "memory is not a substitute for a knowledge file", and it holds what Claude picked up, not the authoritative text of the policy.

quizzes.stem: A department wants a monthly report in one layout, built from figures kept in a shared spreadsheet and delivered to a client in editable form. Which combination fits best?

options.a: A Project for the procedure, an upload for the data and a table for the output
options.b: Research for the data, memory for the procedure and an inline reply for the output
options.c: A skill for the procedure, a connector for the data, an artifact for the output
options.d: Three separate chats, one per stage, with material copied across by hand

explanation.c: A skill carries a repeatable procedure, a connector reads live data, and an artifact is a deliverable someone can open and edit.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "A short answer stays inline in the chat", which does not suit a file to be edited.
explanation.a: Ruled out because "an uploaded file is a copy as of the day you uploaded it", so the monthly figures go stale, and a table suits "Data that another program will read", not a client.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A skill is a reusable procedure Claude pulls in when the task matches", which copying by hand gives up.

quizzes.stem: A new hire installs a free skill found on a public forum. Its page says the skill also needs a custom connector to the hire's work email, and the hire's plan allows both. What is the main risk of the pair?

options.a: The pair would fill the context window with tools and skill text
options.b: The connector could open mail folders that the hire cannot open
options.c: The skill would be shared with the hire's team once installed
options.d: Hidden instructions could pass inbox contents to an outside party

explanation.d:
The page names "prompt injection and data exfiltration as the most significant risks" of skills, and
   "Each connector is an extra route for data and for injected instructions", so the pair joins hidden instructions
   to a way out of the mailbox.
explanation.a:
Ruled out because "Only the pertinent skills enter the context window", and
   On demand is suggested only "when you have ten or more connectors".
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "A connector cannot
   give anyone more access than they already have".
explanation.c:
Ruled out because "Free, Pro and Max users manage only
   their own skills", and on Team and Enterprise plans a skill is shared only "with named colleagues".

quizzes.stem: A team works from a shared drive through a connector the owner enabled. One member asks the same travel question twice and gets last year's allowance once and this year's the next time. What should the owner fix first?

options.a: Ask Claude to name the file it used, so the old figure can be spotted
options.b: Add an instruction telling Claude to prefer the most recent figure
options.c: Switch the connector to On demand so tools stop crowding the chat
options.d: Delete the outdated copies where they are stored, keeping a single version

explanation.d:
"A connector shows Claude what is in the system, mistakes included", so two versions in the drive give
   Claude two figures to quote (page 3).
explanation.a:
Ruled out because a reply that names its
   file only "shows at once when it used an old one", and the old copy stays in the drive to be quoted again.
explanation.b:
Ruled out because "an instruction is a
   request and a deleted file is a guarantee", so a preference leaves the old copy in reach.
explanation.c:
is ruled out because
   On demand is suggested "when you have ten or more connectors, so that the conversation is not crowded with tools",
   which is about loading and not about which version is read.
